methods.title: Kill Hill Giants
methods.summary: Big bones on every kill, plus coins, limpwurt roots and runes.

requirements.text: A Brass key opens the locked door by the giants and saves the walk past the skeletons; it is not required.

rate.assumes: The published 110 kills an hour assumes an adamant or better weapon and an amulet of strength. With your gear the combat model gives the pace; these figures are used only when it cannot run.

trip.note: The Edgeville bank is about a minute from the giants (trapdoor, ladder and the walk inside).

methods.marketDependence: The spot is crowded at busy hours; world hopping is the remedy and is not modelled.

guide.text: Take food from the bank. Keep the Big bones the route needs.
Go to the Hill Giants in the Edgeville Dungeon.
Kill giants until the bag is full of loot or the food runs low.
Bank the loot in Edgeville.
Sell the loot you do not need to keep at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Killing hill giants
sources.used: drops per kill (Mmgtable), published pace, location and banking

sources.title: Hill Giant
sources.used: monster page checked against the drop table

assumptions: Giant keys (1/128) and beginner clues are ignored: the Obor fight and clue rewards are not modelled.
Armour and weapon drops are not picked up.
Drops under 1/16 per kill are shown as upside and never counted on.

methods.title: Kill cows for cowhide
methods.summary: A cowhide on every kill from the Lumbridge cow field; cows hit for 1.

rate.assumes: The published 325 hides an hour assumes mithril or better equipment and a teleport back to the field. The combat model gives the pace for your gear.

trip.note: The Lumbridge bank is on the castle roof: stairs both ways.

guide.text: Go to the cow field north of Lumbridge.
Kill cows and pick up the hides until the bag is full.
Bank the hides in the Lumbridge castle.
Sell the hides at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Killing cows and tanning cowhide
sources.used: cows always drop a cowhide, 8 hitpoints, the field, published pace

assumptions: Hides are sold raw: tanning them is a separate, unmodelled step.
Bones and raw beef are left on the ground to keep the bag for hides.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell cowhide until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Mine iron ore
methods.summary: Iron ore in the Dwarven Mine, banked in Falador.

requirements.note: Carried or wielded: a pickaxe is used by Mining level alone.

requirements.text: Combat level 65 or more keeps the king scorpions from being aggressive.

rate.assumes: 560 ores an hour is the published figure for a rune pickaxe at Mining 41 and more, banking included. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: Falador east bank is the nearest to the Dwarven Mine.

spot.label: Dwarven Mine entrance (the iron rocks are inside)

guide.text: Take your pickaxe from the bank.
Go to the Dwarven Mine north of Falador.
Mine iron ore until the bag is full.
Bank the ore in Falador.
Sell the ore at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Mining iron ore (free-to-play)
sources.used: published pace, gem chances, location, scorpion warning

assumptions: The published pace is scaled down for lower levels and lesser pickaxes by a simple stated rule, not a measured one; an observed pace replaces it.
The tile is the mine entrance; the rocks are a short walk inside.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell iron ore until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Mine coal
methods.summary: Coal in the Dwarven Mine, banked in Falador.

requirements.note: Carried or wielded: a pickaxe is used by Mining level alone.

requirements.text: Combat level 65 or more keeps the king scorpions from being aggressive.

rate.assumes: 230 coal an hour is the published figure for a rune pickaxe at Mining 41 and more. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: Falador east bank is the nearest to the Dwarven Mine.

spot.label: Dwarven Mine entrance (the coal rocks are inside)

guide.text: Take your pickaxe from the bank.
Go to the Dwarven Mine north of Falador.
Mine coal until the bag is full.
Bank the coal in Falador.
Sell the coal at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

assumptions: The wiki lists Mining 35 for coal; the game needs 30. 30 is used as the level that unlocks the rock.
The published pace is scaled by a stated rule for lower levels and lesser pickaxes.
Gems found while mining (about 1/282) are ignored.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell coal until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Chop oak logs
methods.summary: Oak trees beside the Draynor bank: almost no walking.

requirements.note: Carried or wielded: an axe is used by Woodcutting level alone; wielding one needs Attack.

rate.assumes: 800 logs an hour sits inside the wiki's 500 to 1,100 range for the levels and axes it lists. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: The oak tree is just east of the Draynor bank.

spot.label: Oak tree east of Draynor Bank

guide.text: Take your axe from the bank.
Go to the oak tree east of the Draynor bank.
Chop oaks until the bag is full.
Bank the logs.
Sell the logs at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Cutting oak logs
sources.used: published pace range, location beside the bank

assumptions: The tile of the tree is approximate (a few tiles); the arrow stops beside the bank.
Oak leaves are ignored.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell oak logs until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Chop yew logs
methods.summary: Yew trees near the Edgeville bank.

requirements.note: Carried or wielded: an axe is used by Woodcutting level alone; wielding one needs Attack.

rate.assumes: 150 logs an hour sits inside the wiki's 100 to 200 range. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: The Edgeville yews are a short walk from the bank.

methods.marketDependence: Forestry events and crowds change the pace; bots on busy worlds crowd the trees.

guide.text: Take your axe from the bank.
Go to the yew trees near Edgeville.
Chop yews until the bag is full.
Bank the logs.
Sell the logs at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

assumptions: The tile of the trees is approximate (within about ten tiles).
Anima-infused bark from Forestry events is ignored.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell yew logs until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Catch lobsters at Musa Point
methods.summary: Raw lobsters on Karamja; the ferry costs 60 coins a round trip.

requirements.reason: The ferry from Port Sarim, there and back

inputs.note: 60 coins for the ferry per trip of 27 catches

rate.assumes: 222 catches an hour is the published figure with the trips included. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: Ferry both ways and the walk to a bank.

guide.text: Take your lobster pot and the ferry fare.
Take the ferry from Port Sarim to Karamja and go to Musa Point.
Catch lobsters until the bag is full.
Ferry back and bank the lobsters.
Sell the lobsters at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Catching lobsters
sources.used: published pace, the 60 coin ferry per trip, location

assumptions: Raw lobsters are sold raw; cooking them is a separate, unmodelled step.
The bank used is Draynor, the nearest to the Port Sarim dock; the walk is part of the trip overhead.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell raw lobster until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Collect dropped iron ore
methods.summary: Pick up ore another player is power-mining at Al Kharid.

requirements.reason: The Al Kharid toll gate, both ways

rate.assumes: 600 ores an hour needs a world where another player is power-mining. The slow figure is a world with little ore.

trip.note: The Al Kharid bank is about 130 tiles from the mine.

methods.marketDependence: Depends on other players dropping ore; an empty world gives nothing.

guide.text: Go to the Al Kharid mine and find a world where someone is mining.
Pick up the iron ore that is dropped, until the bag is full.
Bank the ore in Al Kharid.
Sell the ore at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

assumptions: The pace depends on other players and cannot be modelled; the range is wide on purpose.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell iron ore until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Buy anti-dragon shields from Oziach
methods.summary: Buy shields from Oziach's shop and sell them at the exchange.

rate.assumes: 3,400 shields an hour is 130 trips of 26 with full focus. The market takes far fewer: the evaluator caps the pace by the hour's trades.

trip.note: Oziach's shop in Edgeville is a few steps from the bank.

methods.marketDependence: The shield trades only about 800 times an hour: the market is the limit, not the shop.

guide.text: Take coins from the bank.
Go to Oziach's shop in Edgeville.
Buy shields, 26 at a time.
Bank the shields.
Sell the shields at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Collecting anti-dragon shields (free-to-play)
sources.used: shop price per 26, restock, published pace

assumptions: The shield usually sells below its guide price: the evaluator uses the sell side of the quote.
The shop price is the wiki's; it is not re-read from the game.

methods.title: Smelt steel bars
methods.summary: Buy iron ore and coal, smelt at the Edgeville furnace, sell the bars.

rate.assumes: 775 bars an hour is the published figure at the Edgeville furnace, 9 bars an inventory. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: The Edgeville furnace is a few steps from the bank.

guide.text: Buy iron ore and coal at the Grand Exchange, or take them from the bank.
Go to the Edgeville furnace.
Smelt 9 iron ore with 18 coal at a time.
Bank the bars.
Sell the bars at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

assumptions: Iron ore and coal are bought at the exchange at the instant-buy price.
A new free-to-play account cannot sell steel bars until its trade restrictions lift.

methods.title: Make pie shells
methods.summary: Use pastry dough on pie dishes and sell the shells.

rate.assumes: 2,450 shells an hour is 175 inventories of 14 with the space bar held. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: The Grand Exchange bank booths are beside the counters.

guide.text: Buy pastry dough and pie dishes at the Grand Exchange.
Withdraw 14 dough and 14 dishes, use the dough on the dishes.
Bank the shells.
Sell the shells at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

assumptions: The pie dish exchange buy limit (500 every four hours) caps the pace; the evaluator applies it.
The 2021 revision is old: the margin is re-read from live prices every time.

methods.title: Buy feather packs
methods.summary: Buy feather packs at Gerrant's Fishy Business and sell the feathers.

inputs.note: Ten packs at a time average 209 coins a pack

rate.assumes: 2,592 packs an hour is the published figure. Slow is 55% and typical 80% of it.

trip.note: Gerrant's shop and the Port Sarim deposit box are close.

guide.text: Take coins from the bank.
Go to Gerrant's shop in Port Sarim.
Buy ten packs at a time and open them.
Bank the feathers.
Sell the feathers at the Grand Exchange.
Buy the supplies you were short of, then go back to your step.

sources.title: Money making guide/Buying feather packs
sources.used: price per pack, 100 feathers a pack, break-even note

assumptions: The wiki notes the method pays only while feathers sell for 3 coins or more; the evaluator reads the live sell side and turns negative when it is lower.
The shop tile is approximate.
